newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - KBB 1996/97 net seen shrinking by 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - KBB 1996/97 net seen shrinking by 40 pct.

text.p: Dutch department stores group Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer NV (KBB) is expected to post a sharply lower 1996/97 net profit, as it forecast in a profit warning in January, analysts said on Monday.

They expect KBB to post an operating profit of 60 million guilders when it releases provisional figures for the 1996/97 period on Thursday, down 39 percent from 1995/96's net profit of 98.6 million guilders.
KBB said in January the reduced profits, of between 55 and 60 million guilders, were likely after lower-than-expected results at its M&S Mode clothing unit at the end of 1996.
"The drama is complete, and we know it," ING analyst Dennis Jullens said, echoing the opinion of many analysts.
"Vendex did very well and there would be some interesting comparisons to make," he added.
Bas Nienhaus, analyst at Stroeve agreed, adding it would be too early for measures taken at M&S to have had an impact.

"Even if they wanted to, they could hardly say anything about M&S at the moment. Once most of the summer clothing has been sold, we'll be able to see if M&S's new team has done things better," Nienhaus said.
He said department stores were likely to have benefitted from a recovery in consumer spending. The Hema chain, he added, were likely to have fared even better after restructuring.

"Results at department store De Bijenkorf are less clear, as sales during the last couple of months are decisive for the chain's possible profit," Nienhaus said, adding the chain's sensitivity to trends made it very vulnerable.
Of the speciality stores, DIY chain Praxis was seen to have performed well and was expected to continue on the same path.
"But looking at the speciality stores as a whole (including M&S), nothing of Praxis' good performance is left," said Desiree Claassen, analyst at Van Lanschot.
Like many analysts, she said she still hoped KBB would divulge more details of the developments at its various units as it had hinted at more than a year ago.
KBB itself declined to confirm how detailed its provisional results would be.
"There is indeed an internal discussion going on to let peolpe peek a little more under the veil," said Matthieu Eichholtz, treasurer at KBB.

"But at this stage, I can't say whether the provisional results will be released under a condensed or in a somewhat broader form. The next annual report might give more details than 1995/96's, but I cannot guarantee that," he said.
